summary.auditScope: All 65 task-instruction-aligned-v1 tasks were manually reviewed against their task instructions and declared inputs, covering all 484 rubric rows and 3,235 criteria.
judgeObservationModel: The judge prompt contains rubric text and extracted output-directory contents, but not the task instructions, local reference inputs, external sources, or model trajectory.
Each criterion is binary, and a rubric row receives zero unless every criterion in that row passes, so one invisible requirement can erase credit for otherwise judgeable work.
Non-SQLite extraction is capped at 200,000 characters per file; SQLite extraction exposes schema and only the first 500 rows per table.

XLSX extraction loses formulas, charts, styles, fills, conditional formatting, and template fidelity; DOCX loses pagination and layout; PDF is text-only; PPTX exposes only text-bearing shapes; IPYNB extraction omits common text/plain and HTML MIME-bundle outputs.
At most eight sorted, deduplicated images are attached, only when a limited visual-keyword regex enables vision; XLSX, PPTX, and PDF visual content is not attached.
systemicFindings: Every task contains at least one correctness or completeness criterion that depends on source data or references absent from the judge context.

Format extraction makes valid spreadsheet charts and styling, PDF graphics/forms, PPTX visuals, DOCX page limits, notebook rich outputs, workbook formulas, and large SQLite/workbook tails unobservable.

Several accepted implementation or file-format alternatives are not equally judgeable, including embedded Excel charts versus separate images, PDF versus DOCX figures, and tracked revisions versus explicit text markers.
One explicit task objective is omitted: the HPC Option D rubric checks feasibility but not the required throughput maximization.
summary.absenceVsNotApplicableReview: No standalone high-confidence issue was retained for absence-versus-not-applicable handling. The reviewed rubrics generally used explicit N/A, No Benchmark, unavailable, or conditional-path language when evidence could legitimately be absent.

issues.finding: The judge cannot reliably verify source-derived eligibility counts, event rates, protocol parameters, subgroup denominators, or missingness results because it receives only output deliverables, not framingham.csv or the proposal CSV.
issues.evidence: judge.py builds the prompt from extract_all_file_contents(output_dir) and the rubric text only. The cited criteria require comparison with Clinical_Study_Proposal_CVD_Prevention.csv and framingham.csv, but expected control totals are not included in the rubric.
issues.recommendedChange: Provide judge-readable extracts of the named inputs or add authoritative expected counts/rates and tolerances to the affected criteria; otherwise limit scoring to reported methodology and internal consistency.

issues.finding: A workbook can assert that Wan Nor Arifin's calculator was used even when it was not; actual use of an external spreadsheet is process evidence absent from deliverables.
issues.evidence: The criterion requires cross-validation with a separately obtained calculator, while the judge sees neither the calculator file nor trajectory. Text extraction can only expose a claim or copied result.
issues.recommendedChange: Score a documented independent cross-check with displayed calculator inputs and outputs, or require the completed calculator workbook as a deliverable; do not score unverifiable tool use.

issues.finding: The judge lacks the protocol, trial data, mapping file, and downloaded UCI dataset needed to validate audit discrepancies, LOCF coverage, site effects, sample sizes, conditional power, and RWE rates.
issues.evidence: The prompt contains only DX24_301_Integrity_Analysis.xlsx text plus rubric wording. Criteria such as 1.0, 1.5, 3.0-3.6, 4.1-4.6, and 5.1-5.8 require recomputation from files never supplied to the judge.
issues.recommendedChange: Attach canonical reference extracts or encode expected source-derived values and tolerances in the rubric. Separate verifiable presentation checks from numerical correctness checks.

issues.finding: A valid forest plot embedded as an Excel chart is invisible to the judge, so the rubric favors a separate image even though the task explicitly permits either method.
issues.evidence: Excel extraction uses pandas.read_excel and serializes cell tables only. collect_image_attachments does not inspect XLSX media or render charts; it supports standalone images, DOCX media, and notebook images.
issues.recommendedChange: Render spreadsheet sheets/charts to images for visual rubrics or require a companion image. Until then, accept the complete subgroup estimate/CI table and interaction p-values as equivalent evidence for an embedded chart.

issues.finding: The judge cannot determine whether bank, GL, AP, aging, journal-entry, and Schedule C amounts are complete and correct against the named inputs.
issues.evidence: Only the three produced deliverables are extracted. Criteria including 0.0, 2.0, 2.9, 3.2-3.6, 4.1-4.4, and 5.1-5.10 require source comparison, but neither source files nor expected values appear in the judge prompt.
issues.recommendedChange: Supply reference tables/control totals to the judge or include expected reconciliation facts and accepted mappings in the rubric; retain internal cross-file consistency checks separately.

issues.finding: The requirement that the workbook use the external AP template and official Schedule C source cannot be established from extracted output text.
issues.evidence: The judge has no trajectory, downloaded AP template, or IRS PDF. A deliverable can reproduce plausible fields and merely claim source use.
issues.recommendedChange: Replace source-use scoring with observable conformance to specified AP fields and official line identifiers, or require the source/template artifacts and citations as deliverables.

issues.finding: The judge cannot validate the true cash balance, complete discrepancy set, AP rollforward, chart-of-accounts names, post-adjustment Schedule C values, or budget overruns against the six task inputs.
issues.evidence: judge.py does not include task inputs. The rubric repeatedly requires supported, traceable, or agreeing values without embedding expected results.
issues.recommendedChange: Provide canonical extracted inputs or expected balances, discrepancy records, and tolerances to the judge; score memo/workbook consistency independently of source correctness.

issues.finding: The judge cannot verify skew-adjusted quantities, reinforcement coverage, local costs, WSDOT prices, item comparability, or contingency classifications against the four local inputs and Contract 24Z011.
issues.evidence: The output workbook is the only extracted evidence. Criteria 0.0-0.6, 1.0-1.7, 2.1-2.5, 3.2-3.8, and 4.1 require source values that are not included in the prompt.
issues.recommendedChange: Provide judge-readable source extracts and the WSDOT comparison rows, or embed expected quantities, bar totals, comparable items, and pricing tolerances in the rubric.

issues.finding: Most correctness checks depend on the scope memo, FDOT workbook, labor rates, CDOT and WisDOT data, none of which the judge receives.
issues.evidence: Criteria require independent quantity derivations, specific source hierarchy, crew rates, unit-price comparisons, construction staging, and reconciled totals. The judge prompt contains only the produced workbook and memo.
issues.recommendedChange: Include canonical source tables and expected quantity controls with the judge request, or convert unsupported correctness checks into observable documentation/internal-consistency checks.

issues.finding: Although several expected quantities are embedded in Row 1, the judge still cannot verify complete CSV coverage, authorized scope, source hierarchy, unit prices, risk grounding, or lifecycle inputs against the project files and external cost books.
issues.evidence: Criteria 0.1, 0.3, 1.5, 2.0-2.4, 3.0-3.1, 4.1-4.4, and 5.4 refer to materials absent from the judge prompt.
issues.recommendedChange: Retain embedded expected quantity checks, and add authoritative lists/control totals for all remaining source-dependent criteria or provide the actual references to the judge.

issues.finding: The judge cannot determine whether the DOCX memo is one page or less because DOCX extraction discards pagination and layout.
issues.evidence: mammoth.convert_to_markdown supplies document text but no rendered pages or page count. A multi-page memo and a one-page memo with the same text appear equivalent.
issues.recommendedChange: Render DOCX pages to images/PDF and pass page count, or replace the page-limit criterion with a word/character limit that the extractor can measure.

issues.finding: The judge cannot validate Option D constraints, 36-month allocations, database-derived trends, SQL table/column validity, lead times, or Epoch benchmark facts because the six inputs and external dataset are absent.
issues.evidence: Only output files are extracted. Criteria 2.0-2.4 require every database project; 4.0-4.5 require SQL valid against the real database; 5.6 requires records from Epoch AI. Only a few hardware constants are embedded in Row 0.
issues.recommendedChange: Pass reference data and a disposable SQLite copy to deterministic checks, then give those results to the judge. Embed expected constraints and peer records where direct input access is not possible.

issues.finding: The instructions require Option D to maximize research throughput while satisfying all current requirements, but the rubric only checks feasibility and constraint compliance. A materially dominated feasible configuration can receive full credit.
issues.evidence: Row 1 checks availability, budget, annual caps, contingency, facility, sustainability, and access constraints; no criterion compares verified throughput or cost-efficiency with feasible alternatives.
issues.recommendedChange: Add a criterion requiring a stated optimization objective and evidence that Option D is non-dominated or throughput-maximizing under the documented discrete purchasing constraints; accept equivalent optimization methods.

issues.finding: Validity and source-grounded behavior of workload_impact.sql cannot be judged from SQL text alone; it must be executed against workload_requirements.db.
issues.evidence: The extractor presents the .sql file as text, while the database is not supplied in the judge prompt and the judge performs no SQL execution. Plausible but invalid table names or wrong results can pass semantically.
issues.recommendedChange: Execute the script deterministically against a copy of the database, capture schema/errors/results, and score those artifacts; reserve the LLM for explanation and query-intent review.

issues.finding: The judge cannot verify the exhaustive data audit, workload/database calculations, vendor repricing, LBNL evidence, HERD peer comparison, or corrected schedule against the four local inputs and external report.
issues.evidence: Criteria repeatedly require every roll-up, every workload, all original activities, and specific source-grounded values. The judge sees only the produced Markdown, workbook, and CSV, with no reference files or expected results.
issues.recommendedChange: Give the judge canonical extracts and expected audit discrepancies/control totals, and validate the schedule/database-derived populations deterministically before LLM review.

issues.finding: The judge cannot confirm server completeness and tiers, database risks, vendor proposals, budget lines, NIST questions, AWS instance eligibility, or incident correlations because none of the source systems or external CSVs are supplied.
issues.evidence: Criteria 0.0-0.3, 1.0-1.3, 2.0-2.3, 4.1-4.3, 5.0-5.3, and 6.0-6.3 depend on exact source rows. The rubric includes rules but not the actual populations or expected outputs.
issues.recommendedChange: Provide extracted source tables and external reference rows, or run deterministic reconciliation checks and include their results in the judge evidence.

issues.finding: The judge lacks the incident log, budget workbook, inventory, NIST Core, and AWS calculator data needed to validate the candidate population, costs, project coverage, budget availability, and gap mappings.
issues.evidence: The rubric asks for complete top-10, median, every candidate, every pending project, and official NIST mappings, but output deliverables are the only evidence sent to the judge.
issues.recommendedChange: Supply reference extracts and expected populations/control totals; use deterministic joins and cost calculations for completeness and reserve LLM scoring for rationale quality.

issues.finding: Red conditional formatting in the Gap_Register sheet is not visible in the Excel text extraction, so a correctly formatted workbook and an unformatted one are indistinguishable.
issues.evidence: pandas.read_excel emits cell values as CSV and discards fills, conditional-formatting rules, and styles. No XLSX rendering or style inspection is attached.
issues.recommendedChange: Inspect XLSX conditional-formatting rules programmatically or render the sheet. Alternatively remove the formatting criterion and score an explicit UNBUDGETED/high-severity flag column.

issues.finding: The judge can read the produced dashboard database but cannot compare it with the source inventory database, gateway log, ticket export, escalation email, CAB template, or Cisco guidance.
issues.evidence: Criteria require every gateway session, every full version, specific cross-source matches, every template field, exact database joins, and full-date totals. Those source populations are absent from the prompt.
issues.recommendedChange: Pass normalized source extracts and template fields to the judge or compute deterministic expected counts, mappings, and database validation results before semantic review.

issues.finding: The judge cannot validate device coverage/classification, disputed-readiness root causes, sprint constraints, database ticket patterns, staff capacity, or cited post-EOL risks against the inventory, database, manager email, budget, briefing, and external guide.
issues.evidence: The criteria require every device, every staff member, actual top-five ticket subcategories, exact manager constraints, and source-grounded compliance claims. Only the three deliverables are passed to the judge.
issues.recommendedChange: Provide normalized source tables and authoritative hardware requirement data, plus deterministic coverage/count checks, to the judge.

issues.finding: The PPTX evaluator cannot see embedded charts, images, or visual timeline/budget treatments, so a text-only slide deck can look equivalent to a well-designed visual deck and valid image-only slides can look empty.
issues.evidence: PPTX extraction iterates shapes and appends only shape.text. The image collector does not inspect PPTX media or render slides.
issues.recommendedChange: Render every slide to an image and attach the slide images for deck rubrics, while retaining text extraction for citations and numbers.

issues.finding: The judge cannot verify case facts, discrepancies, legal analysis, fees, mandatory assessments, database changes, or register consistency against the notes, source CMS, fee schedule, defense memo, form, and AOC instructions.
issues.evidence: All substantive criteria require exact source materials, but the prompt includes only produced CSVs, PDFs, and updated database. The original CMS is also needed to distinguish correct updates from pre-existing data.
issues.recommendedChange: Provide source extracts and deterministic database diff results; embed authoritative legal/fee expectations or include the cited sources in judge evidence.

issues.finding: Filled values in the supplied official PDF form may be AcroForm widget values or annotations that pdfplumber does not extract, and the judge receives no rendered PDF pages. Valid completed forms can therefore appear blank or indistinguishable from the template.
issues.evidence: convert_file_to_text uses pdfplumber page.extract_text(layout=True) only. It does not read form fields or attach PDF page images.
issues.recommendedChange: Extract AcroForm field names/values and render each order page to images before judging official-form use and completion.

issues.finding: The judge cannot verify the six dispute rows, weather calculations, supervisor-note verdicts, deadlines, rate plans, PUC contact information, EIA benchmarks, or policy conclusions against the four local files and external EIA data.
issues.evidence: The rubric requires exact customer-level and source-level results but embeds none of the expected values and the judge prompt excludes inputs.
issues.recommendedChange: Pass canonical dispute, billing, weather, rights, note, and benchmark extracts to the judge or add expected values/tolerances to each numerical criterion.

issues.finding: The judge cannot determine whether every field discrepancy was found or reconciled correctly because the CRM, ERP, customer master, checklist template, and ten authoritative scanned order forms are not included.

issues.finding: The judge cannot validate portfolio totals, watch-list completeness, CDFI scores, rate-shock calculations, FDIC benchmarks, policy thresholds, or capital allocation against the local portfolio/applications/template and external FDIC/OCC sources.

issues.finding: The DOCX extractor cannot determine whether the strategic memo is approximately two to three pages.

issues.finding: Neither the five-page DOCX limit nor the requirement that the Go/No-Go matrix occupy a single page is observable after DOCX-to-Markdown extraction.
issues.evidence: Mammoth strips page layout and pagination; the judge sees continuous text.

issues.finding: Executed notebook outputs stored in standard Jupyter data bundles are omitted from text extraction, so visible tables/statistics may not reach the judge.
